subject: SIG: Data handling — prompt log retention & training exclusion flow
messages:

Subject: SIG: initial questions on prompt logs & training

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for taking the time on Friday. HealthVera's infosec team has started our SIG review and we need a short follow-up specifically on the way Redwood handles conversational prompts/payloads and whether customer inputs are ever used for model training. A few concrete asks: 

- Do you persist raw prompt text or structured request metadata? If so, what's the default retention window and are there per-customer controls?
- Are prompt logs ever used to train or fine-tune models (internal or third-party)? If yes, what opt-out mechanisms exist?
- For Dedicated/Private deployments, can customers force logs to be ephemeral or filtered before persistence?

We would appreciate a concise written response and any supporting exhibits for our SIG evidence package. Our deadline for the next round is EOD Thursday (27 May).

Best,
Julie Thompson
Director, Security Operations
HealthVera

Attachment: HealthVera_SIG_Request_v1.pdf (application/pdf)
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Hi Julie — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers up front, and I attached a short exhibit that our compliance team compiles for SIG/CAIQ requests ("redwood-sig-data-handling-exhibit.pdf"). Please see details below; happy to hop on a short call if you'd like a walkthrough before Thursday.

- Retention: By default, hosted API prompt/request logs are retained for 30 days for debugging and abuse detection. Metadata (timestamps, route/model used, token counts) are kept for 365 days for billing and usage analytics.

- Training: We do not use customer prompt text to train general-purpose public models unless a customer has explicitly opted in via contractual language and account-level setting. For customers that opt in, we surface the opt-in and provide exportable records.

- Per-customer controls / Private: For Dedicated and Private deployments, operators can configure retention to zero (ephemeral mode) or route logs to customer-managed sinks only. We support a "training_exclusion" flag at the tenant level which prevents any downstream ingestion into model-improvement pipelines.

- Redaction and filters: We offer a configurable pre-ingest redaction step (PII regex rules + user-supplied redaction rules) for hosted customers. Our default offboard playbook ensures all retained prompt artifacts for offboarded accounts are deleted within the contractual window.

Attachments included: redwood-sig-data-handling-exhibit.pdf (PDF) — covers retention windows, opt-in process, and audit logs; training-optout-configuration.md (text) — a short guide for our enterprise customers explaining the training_exclusion flag and steps to enable it.

Next steps: Marcus (cc'd) can coordinate a short walkthrough of the exhibit or provide tenant-level screenshots of the Admin console if that helps your Signoff. Aditya can add a sentence on how we segregate telemetry from training pipelines.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Manager, Compliance & Trust
Redwood Inference

Thanks, Kimberly — that's helpful. A couple of clarifying points from our reviewers: 

1) You mentioned the "training_exclusion" flag — can you confirm whether that applies retroactively to previously collected prompts or only to future ingestion? We need to know whether enabling it will remove previously-seen text from model-improvement queues.

2) For hosted customers who do NOT opt in, are there any automated de-identification / redaction steps applied before text is ever persisted? If not, are you willing to include a contractual carve-out that we can toggle for sensitive routes?

3) Can you provide a sample audit log entry (sanitized) that shows the record kept when a customer toggles the exclusion flag or when a deletion job runs? That would help our SIG evidence.

If you can get answers and either the exhibit update or one more brief note by EOD Thursday our reviewer will likely sign off.

Best,
Julie
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Julie — quick follow-up with the specifics your reviewers requested. I pulled Aditya and Marcus in to confirm technical and product behavior; below are concrete, copy-ready statements you can drop into the SIG exhibit.

1) Training_exclusion behavior: When enabled at the tenant level, the training_exclusion flag applies prospectively to downstream model-improvement ingestion pipelines. For data collected prior to flag enablement, we run an opt-out purge process:

   - We mark all candidate records with the tenant_id and a deletion_request timestamp.
   - A deletion job then (a) removes raw text from our short-term debug store, (b) truncates retained metadata in analytic store to non-identifying aggregates, and (c) flags any queued training bundles for removal before model pipeline consumption.

   - We provide an audit artifact (see sample below) showing tenant_id, action (training_exclusion_enabled), operator, and timestamp. Note the purge for historic data completes within 7 calendar days for hosted accounts and can be SLA'd for Dedicated customers in the contract.

2) Automated redaction before persistence: For hosted accounts, we do not automatically redact natural language text by default (we retain raw text for 30 days). However, we provide a built-in pre-ingest redaction engine that can be enabled per-route to remove PII patterns (SSN, credit-card, emails) and custom regex at the customer request. We will include a contractual Addendum language to implement a route-level mandatory redaction requirement for HealthVera-sensitive endpoints.

3) Sample audit record (sanitized):

   On Thu, 27 May 2027 at 15:00:12 -0700 Redwood Compliance <compliance@redwood.ai> wrote:
   action: training_exclusion_enabled
   tenant_id: HV-10023
   operator: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
   timestamp: 2027-05-27T15:00:12-07:00
   result: queued_historic-purge (expected completion: 2027-06-03)

   This artifact will be stored in the tenant's audit bucket and is exportable via the Admin console or the Compliance API.

Operational notes: Dedicated/Private deployments support a default-offline mode where no host-managed prompt text is persisted; in those setups, we provide a signed attestation and configuration checklist as part of the onboarding packet.

I'll attach an updated exhibit with the sample audit record and proposed contractual addendum language. Marcus will follow up about scheduling a 30-minute walkthrough of the Admin console to show the training_exclusion toggle and deletion job logs.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Manager, Compliance & Trust
Redwood Inference
